title: वैदिक सामाजिक संरचना र लैङ्गिकताको सवाल Vaidik Samajik Samrachana ra Laingikatako Sawal
nepali: वैदिक सामाजिक संरचनालाई प्राचीन ग्रन्थ वेदले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने कालखण्डकोपरावर्तित स्वरूपको रूपमा बुझिन्छ । यस आलेखको उद्देश्य त्यही प्राचीन ग्रन्थ वेदले प्रतिनिधित्वगर्ने कालखण्डको सामाजिक संरचनाभित्र  पुरुषत्व तथा नारीत्व र दाम्पत्य सम्बन्धकोे विश्लेषणगर्दै लैङ्गिकता निर्माणका तथ्यहरूसँग सैदान्तिक बहसमा केन्द्रित सैद्धान्तिक मान्यताहरूकोसादृश्यता खोज्ने रहेको छ । उल्लिखित उद्देश्य प्राप्तिको लागि वेद, वेदको ऐतिहासिकता,ऐतिहासिक सन्दर्भहरू, विभिन्न  लैङ्गिक अध्ययनहरूलाई सूचनाको स्रोतको रूपमा लिइएको छ ।यस अध्ययनमा मुख्य गरी द्वितीय स्रोतमा आधारित तथ्यहरूको बढी प्रयोग गरिएको छ ।संकलित तथ्यहरूलाई विश्लेषणका लागि ऐतिहासिक अन्तर्वस्तु विश्लेषण विधिलाई प्रयोगमाल्याइएको छ । वेदकालीन सामाजिक संरचना पशुपालन र पितृसत्तात्मक स्वरूपको भएकालेवेदकालीन परिवार एवम् राज्यमा पुरुष वंश र नेतृत्व स्थापित भएको पाइयो । उत्पादन तथाश्रममूलक कार्य अन्तर्गत घरायसी कार्यमा महिलाको र बाह्य काममा पुरुषको संलग्नता बढी रहने गरेको देखिए पनि यज्ञ, संस्कार, युद्ध एवम् राजनीतिक कार्यमा महिला पुरुष दुवैको सहभागिता रहेको देखिएको छ । साधन स्रोतको विस्तार र राज्य व्यवस्थाको निर्माणसँगैनेतृत्वमा स्थापित भएको राजन्य एवं पुरोहितवर्गले वैदिक आर्यहरूको प्रजातीय शुद्धता कायमराख्ने हेतुले निर्माण गरेका विभिन्न संस्कारजन्य विधि विधानहरूप्रतिको विश्वास र अभ्यासबाटवेदकालीन  समाजमा एकीकृत भूमिका, निष्ठा र मर्यादा सहितको दाम्पत्य सम्बन्धको विकासगराएको देखिन्छ ।
american_english: Vedic social structure is understood as the reflected form of the epoch represented by the ancient text, the Veda. The objective of this article is, while analyzing manhood and womanhood and the conjugal relationship within the social structure of the epoch represented by that same ancient text, the Veda, to seek the similarity between the theoretical propositions centered in the theoretical debate and the facts of gender construction. For attaining the stated objective, the Veda, the historicity of the Veda, historical contexts, and various gender studies have been taken as sources of information. In this study, facts based mainly on secondary sources have been used to a greater extent. For the analysis of the collected facts, the method of historical content analysis has been brought into use. Since the Vedic social structure was of a pastoral and patriarchal character, it was found that male lineage and leadership were established in the Vedic family and state. Although under production and labor-based work it was seen that women's involvement in domestic work and men's in external work remained greater, the participation of both women and men is seen in yajña, rites, war and political work. It is seen that, along with the expansion of the resource base and the building of the state order, the rājanya and priestly class, established in leadership, through the belief in and practice of the various ritual codes they created to maintain the racial purity of the Vedic Aryans, brought about the development in Vedic society of a conjugal relationship with an integrated role, fidelity and dignity.
british_english: Vedic social structure is understood as the reflected form of the epoch represented by the ancient text, the Veda. The aim of this article is, while analysing manliness and womanliness and the married relationship within the social structure of the epoch represented by that same ancient text, the Veda, to seek the resemblance between the theoretical assumptions centred in the theoretical debate and the facts of gender construction. For the attainment of the stated aim, the Veda, the historicity of the Veda, historical contexts and various gender studies have been taken as sources of information. In this study, facts based mainly on secondary sources have been used to a greater measure. For the analysis of the collected facts, the method of historical content analysis has been brought into play. As Vedic social structure was of a pastoral and patriarchal character, it was found that the male line and leadership had been established in the Vedic family and state. Although under production and labour-based work it was observed that women's involvement in domestic work and men's in work outside remained greater, the participation of both women and men is seen in yajña, rites, war and political affairs. It is seen that, along with the expansion of the resource base and the building of the state order, the rājanya and priestly order, established in leadership, by virtue of their belief in and practice of the various ritual codes they framed to maintain the racial purity of the Vedic Aryans, brought about the development in Vedic society of a conjugal relationship marked by an integrated role, fidelity and decorum.
australian_english: Vedic social structure is read as the mirrored form of the era the ancient text, the Veda, stands for. The aim of this article is, while looking into manhood and womanhood and married life within the social structure of the era that same ancient text, the Veda, stands for, to chase down how far the theoretical propositions at the centre of the theoretical argument match up with the facts of gender construction. To reach the stated aim, the Veda, the historicity of the Veda, historical contexts and various gender studies have been taken as sources of information. In this study, facts based mainly on secondary sources have been drawn on the most. To analyse the collected facts, the method of historical content analysis has been put to work. Because the Vedic social structure was pastoral and patriarchal in shape, it was found that the male line and leadership had taken hold in the Vedic family and state. Even though under production and labour-based work women's involvement in domestic chores and men's in outside work look to have been greater, the participation of both women and men is seen in yajña, rites, war and political business. It is seen that, along with the expansion of the resource base and the building of the state order, the rājanya and priestly group, settled in leadership, through the belief in and practice of the various ritual codes they put together to keep the Vedic Aryans racially pure, brought about in Vedic society the development of a conjugal relationship with a unified role, loyalty and standing.
informal_english: People take Vedic social structure to be the mirror image of the age that the ancient text, the Vedas, stands for. This article wants to look at manhood and womanhood and husband–wife relations inside the social structure of that same age the Vedas stand for, and, doing that, to hunt for how far the theory that comes up in the gender debate matches the facts of how gender gets made. To get there, the Vedas, the historicity of the Vedas, historical contexts and different gender studies have all been taken as sources of information. This study mainly leans on facts drawn from secondary sources. The collected facts have been put through the historical content analysis method for analysis. Because the Vedic social structure was pastoral and patriarchal, it was found that male line and leadership got established in the Vedic family and state. Even though under production and labour women were seen to be more into household work and men more into outside work, both women and men were seen taking part in yajña, rites, war and political work. It looks like that, along with resources spreading and the state system taking shape, the belief in and practice of the various ritual procedures that the rajanya and priestly class, once settled in leadership, made to keep the Vedic Aryans racially pure, brought about in Vedic society a husband–wife relationship with a unified role, loyalty and dignity.
translator_notes: Source is a theoretical article on Vedic social structure and gender; key terms (yajña, rājanya) preserved; secondary-source emphasis and sentence order kept as in source.
